Chapter 11. Sacred Places, Shifting Borders—Land, Identity, and the Meaning of Home.
For Christians in the Middle East, land isn’t just about soil or boundaries. It’s something deeper—a source of identity, a living bridge to ancestors, and the very ground where their faith takes root. But the idea of home? It’s always under pressure. Borders shift, wars break out, people get displaced, and life changes faster than anyone expects.
Picture a village perched high on a hillside. There’s a farmer, quietly caring for his olive trees. Each one was planted by his father or maybe even his grandfather. These olives aren’t just a harvest—they’re a symbol of endurance. When times get tough, those trees remind everyone that life, somehow, keeps going.
Then, imagine a family coming back to their old village after years spent in exile. Their house is crumbling, weeds have taken over the fields, but they roll up their sleeves and dive in—clearing away debris, planting new seeds, bringing new hope. The children wander through empty streets, listening as their parents share memories of what the village used to be. For the parents, every stone they move and seed they plant is about more than rebuilding walls. It’s about reclaiming their place in the world.
Now, shift to a city that’s cut up by walls and checkpoints. Here, a young man faces the daily grind of living under occupation. It’s hard to feel at home when every step is watched, when every choice is shaped by forces you can’t control. Still, he finds little pockets of peace—in the hush of a church, the laughter shared with friends, the rituals that quietly connect him to something bigger than himself.
Most people don’t realize just how much the meaning of home can shift. Home isn’t always a single place. Sometimes it’s a memory, sometimes it’s hope, and sometimes it’s a sense of loss you carry with you. These stories of land and identity remind us that belonging is about more than where you live—it’s about how you live. It’s the connections you make, the traditions you hold onto, and the dreams you keep alive.
